factors.name: Size and parallel branching
factors.summary: Measures of net size and of splitting and parallel structure load very highly (0.92–0.97), joined by Maximum connector degree (0.80) and, more moderately, Connector Mismatch (0.56, communality only 0.37). In this dataset, larger nets have more parallel splits, more arcs per node and larger connectors. Density loads negatively (-0.43), and Sequentiality (0.35) also loads moderately, but both are assigned elsewhere.

factors.name: Connector degree and density
factors.summary: Average connector degree (0.90) and Density (0.81) define this factor, which reflects how strongly arcs are concentrated relative to the number of nodes. Maximum connector degree has a secondary loading (0.41) next to its main loading on Factor 1. Connector Heterogeneity loads negatively (-0.49) and cross-loads with Factor 4, so nets with high connector degree tend to have a less mixed set of connector types.

factors.name: Sequential, separable structure
factors.summary: Separability (0.93) and Sequentiality (0.76) both describe chain-like nets with many articulation points avoided and many arcs between non-connector nodes, i.e. little interleaving of branching. Only two measures carry the factor, but their meanings fit together well. Sequentiality also loads moderately on Factor 1 (0.35).

factors.name: Connector type mix (weak)
factors.summary: This factor is carried by Connector Heterogeneity alone (0.62), which also cross-loads negatively on Factor 2 (-0.49). Its eigenvalue (0.68) is below 1, and it explains only 4.4% of the variance; it was retained beyond the suggested three factors. It is best read as a measure-specific factor rather than a substantive dimension.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO is 0.83, though per-measure MSA is only just above 0.6 for Connector Heterogeneity, Average connector degree and Density. With varimax rotation, four factors explain 86% of the variance. A dominant size and parallel-branching factor (50%) is followed by a connector degree and density factor (17%) and a sequentiality and separability factor (15%). A fourth factor, retained beyond the suggested three, is essentially Connector Heterogeneity alone. Every measure is assigned to a factor, and the only cross-loading is that of Connector Heterogeneity, between Factors 4 and 2.
caveats: Four factors were extracted although three were suggested, and the eigenvalue of the fourth is 0.68, so Factor 4 is weak and possibly spurious.
Connector Heterogeneity is undefined for nets without connectors, and how such cases were handled is not stated, which may affect Factors 2 and 4.
Connector Mismatch has a low communality (0.37), so it is only partly explained by the factor solution.
Several Factor 1 loadings near 0.97 indicate that those measures are nearly redundant in this dataset.
Number of duplicate tasks was removed as constant, so the analysis says nothing about label duplication.
The structure reflects nets produced by particular discovery algorithms and may not generalise to other model collections or to other rotations or factor counts.
